entries.reason: Tile animation and render traversal are map-owned systems with graphics as a borrowed service.
evidence: docs/dev/重构代码质量与系统完整性规范.md
entries.entity_scope: Visible TileLayer entities in the current ECS/map world.
entries.view: Generation-checked TileLayer view plus renderer-owned graphics batch context.
entries.read_set: Tile layer visibility, tile animation clocks, atlas metadata and map transforms.
entries.write_set: Tile animation time state and graphics batch submissions.
entries.structural_changes: No layer creation/destruction during traversal; callers own structural edits.
entries.events: No gameplay events; visible output is the rendered tile batch.
entries.services: Borrowed Graphics backend and injected dt for animation update.

entries.reason: Map::publishCollision consumes the multi-listener ITileCollisionSink socket through cap::forEach and the new script seam answers it through cap::addListener, so the same capability appears on both faces; recording them makes the next provider or consumer declare itself. The scope is this one file, not src/modules/map/**: the editing and level satellites are separately built modules whose faces must not be attributed to this entry.
binds: eve.provider.publishFor('ITileCollisionSink', name, instance) -> replaceTileCollision({ layer = { id, generation }, rects = [{ x, y, width, height }] }); eve.TileLayer.getEntityId()/getEntityGeneration()
entries.thread_affinity: Map owner thread (the Squirrel owning thread for the instance); the sink is called synchronously from publishCollision and no script value is retained across calls

trim.absent_profile: Profiles without map drop the module and its sink listeners; a script that published a collision sink sees the provider go away with the module and the map keeps its own collisionRects_ authority

cost_notes: replaceTileCollision marshals one rect array per layer publication; map keeps collisionRects_ as the authority and a sink failure stays observable through scriptTileCollisionSinkFailures().
